review_notes: Read the whole target file plus the definitions of upperUnit, lowerUnit, blockDiagonalUnit (Whitehead.lean), the upperUnit_/lowerUnit_ lemmas (ElementaryWhitehead.lean), RelativeElementary.lean, and Mathlib's Matrix.map_single. The simp interface of the block units has no @[simp] lemmas for the coercions or for the inverse and zero rules. Only mapRingHom_upperUnit and mapRingHom_lowerUnit are simp. I could not run Lean, so I make no claims about loops or simp failures. The proposed lemmas are untested and may need small adjustments. Whether upperUnit_add should be simp is a judgment call, and I recommend against it.

findings.excerpt: simp only [blockDiagonalUnit, upperUnit, lowerUnit, neg_sub, neg_neg, Matrix.mul_sub,
findings.problem: upperUnit, lowerUnit and blockDiagonalUnit are structures with no simp lemmas for their coercion to a matrix. Every proof that needs the underlying matrix has to unfold the definitions by name. Here a long simp only list includes the three definitions plus fromBlocks_multiply. The same pattern appears at line 174 (`simp [upperUnit]`) and in ElementaryWhitehead.lean (`simp [upperUnit]`, `simp [lowerUnit]`) and Whitehead.lean (`simp [blockDiagonalUnit, upperUnit, lowerUnit, swapUnit, ...]`). Unfolding the definitions exposes the Units.mk fields rather than a canonical form.
findings.proposed_change: In Whitehead.lean, next to the definitions, add @[simp] lemmas `Matrix.fromBlocks 1 a 0 1` for `((upperUnit a : (BlockMatrix ..)ˣ) : Matrix ..)`, `fromBlocks 1 0 (-a) 1` for lowerUnit, and `fromBlocks g 0 0 ↑g⁻¹` for blockDiagonalUnit (coe_upperUnit, coe_lowerUnit, coe_blockDiagonalUnit; each should hold by rfl). Add the matching inverse coercion lemmas such as `↑(upperUnit a)⁻¹ = fromBlocks 1 (-a) 0 1`. Then `simp only [coe_upperUnit, coe_lowerUnit, coe_blockDiagonalUnit, Units.val_mul, Matrix.fromBlocks_multiply, ...]` replaces the unfolding at lines 119–123 and 174, and the definitions stay irreducible-looking to downstream simp calls.
findings.benefit: Downstream block-matrix computations get a stable normal form, namely `fromBlocks` on the underlying matrix, without unfolding the structure definitions. Proofs such as blockDiagonalUnit_eq_five become shorter and less fragile if the field layout of the definitions changes.

findings.excerpt: change upperUnit (-1 : Matrix ι ι R) = (upperUnit (1 : Matrix ι ι R))⁻¹
findings.problem: The group-law facts about upperUnit and lowerUnit are not simp-usable. upperUnit_zero and lowerUnit_zero (`upperUnit 0 = 1`) are not tagged @[simp], although they are terminating, canonical and assumption-free. There is no lemma `upperUnit (-a) = (upperUnit a)⁻¹`, and none for lowerUnit. So hUpperInv is re-proved by hand with Subtype.ext, change, Units.ext and `simp [upperUnit]`. The zero case at line 45 also goes through convert, Subtype.ext and an explicit `exact upperUnit_zero`.
findings.proposed_change: In ElementaryWhitehead.lean, mark upperUnit_zero and lowerUnit_zero @[simp]. Add `upperUnit_neg (a) : upperUnit (-a) = (upperUnit a)⁻¹` and `lowerUnit_neg`. Both hold by Units.ext on the definitions, since the stored inverse is `fromBlocks 1 (-a) 0 1`. They should probably be @[simp] too: the right-hand side's argument gets smaller, so there is no cycle, and `inv` of a unit atom is a normal form. Keep upperUnit_add and lowerUnit_add as plain rewriting lemmas, because splitting sums into products would not be a normal form. Then hUpperInv reduces to `upperUnit_neg`, and the main theorem needs no `change`.
findings.benefit: The unit-valued block API becomes a proper additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism interface. Zero and negation simplify automatically, which removes the ad hoc unfolding proof at lines 170–174 and gives a reusable inverse rule for the lower block as well.

findings.excerpt: have heq : (fun row col => ((Matrix.single i j c row col : I) : R)) =
findings.problem: Entrywise coercion of `Matrix.single i j (c : I)` into R is proved by an identical local `heq` (ext, `simp only [Matrix.single_apply]`, `split_ifs <;> rfl`) in both theorems (lines 58–62 and 97–101). The shape `fun row col => ((single i j c row col : I) : R)` is a Matrix.map with a coercion, which is not stated in a form existing simp lemmas fire on. The unmapped `Matrix.map_single` is @[simp], and RelativeElementary.lean already uses it for ring homs.
findings.proposed_change: State the coefficient matrix as `b.map (Subtype.val)` or `b.map I.subtype`, and use the existing @[simp] `Matrix.map_single` (which needs only ZeroHomClass for the coercion). Or add one shared lemma for the coercion of `single i j c`, instead of two private copies of `heq`. Then `simpa using upperUnit_single i j (c : R)` handles the basis case and `Matrix.map_add`/`Matrix.map_zero` handle the other two induction cases.
findings.benefit: Removes duplicated ad hoc normalization in both theorems and routes coercion of single-entry matrices through the library's canonical simp lemma. The heq in the h_add case also becomes a simp consequence rather than a rewritten fun-equality.
